itineraires.name: La Loire à Vélo
itineraires.alt: A group of cyclists on the banks of the Loire
itineraires.desc: France's best-known cycle route follows the Loire upstream from Nantes: châteaux, vineyards and riverside villages, on a flat and very well signposted route. Perfect for a first cycling holiday, with family or friends.

page.h1: La Loire à Vélo from Nantes
page.title: Loire à Vélo from Nantes: Stages & Bike Hire | Bike'N Tour
page.meta: La Loire à Vélo from Nantes: 165 km to Saumur in 3 to 4 days, suggested stages, train back and touring bike or e-bike hire.
page.intro: La Loire à Vélo (EuroVelo 6) is France's most popular cycle route. From Nantes, it follows the river upstream to Angers and Saumur on a flat, very well signposted route that is largely traffic-free: the ideal trip for your first cycling holiday, with family or friends.

stages.texte: Out of Nantes along the Loire, past Mauves-sur-Loire and its riverside guinguettes, and Oudon with its tower.
Champtoceaux, the hillsides of the Layon and Anjou, then Angers and its castle.
Tufa-stone villages, cave dwellings and a finish at the foot of Saumur castle.

highlights: The Château des ducs de Bretagne at the start
Angers castle and the Apocalypse Tapestry
The cave dwellings and Saumur castle
page.back: Direct trains from Saumur and Angers to Nantes (TER, bikes accepted depending on the season), or one-way hire on request.

faq.question: How many days does it take to cycle the Loire à Vélo from Nantes to Saumur?
faq.reponse: Allow 3 to 4 days for the 165 km between Nantes and Saumur, at 40 to 60 km a day. The Nantes – Angers weekend (110 km) takes 2 days.

faq.question: Is the Loire à Vélo suitable for children?
faq.reponse: Yes: the route is flat and often traffic-free. With children, plan on 20 to 30 km a day; we hire out kids' bikes, baby seats and trailers.

itineraires.name: La Vélodyssée
itineraires.short: To the ocean and the Vendée
itineraires.alt: Cyclists with panniers on a country track
itineraires.desc: From Nantes, La Vélodyssée heads to the ocean through the Pays de Retz, then follows the Vendée coast: marshes, beaches and pine-forest trails, with a fresh sea breeze thrown in.

page.title: Vélodyssée from Nantes: Pornic, Les Sables | Bike'N Tour
page.meta: La Vélodyssée from Nantes: the estuary, Pornic and the Vendée coast to Les Sables-d'Olonne (≈ 240 km). Stages, train back and bike hire.
page.intro: La Vélodyssée (EuroVelo 1) runs from Roscoff to Hendaye. From Nantes, it reaches the ocean along the Loire estuary, then heads down the Côte de Jade and the Vendée coast: marshes, beaches, pine forests and fishing ports.

stages.texte: The Estuaire art trail, the Martinière canal and the fishermen's lift-net huts.
Saint-Brevin-les-Pins, the ocean at last, then the Côte de Jade to Pornic's old harbour.
The Bay of Bourgneuf and the Breton-Vendée marshes.
Pine-forest trails, Saint-Gilles-Croix-de-Vie and the finish at Les Sables.

highlights: The artworks of the Estuaire trail
The pine forest of the Côte de Lumière
page.back: Trains from Pornic to Nantes (40 min) and from Les Sables-d'Olonne to Nantes, or one-way hire on request.

faq.question: Can I cycle from Nantes to Pornic in a weekend?
faq.reponse: Yes: 100 km in 2 days, with a night in Paimbœuf or Corsept, and a train back from Pornic to Nantes in about 40 minutes.

itineraires.name: La Régalante
itineraires.alt: Three cyclists on a forest track
itineraires.desc: The new cycle route linking Nantes to Mont-Saint-Michel inland: greenways, historic towns like Châteaubriant, Vitré and Fougères, and very little climbing.

page.h1: La Régalante, from Nantes to Mont-Saint-Michel
page.title: La Régalante by Bike: Nantes – Mont-Saint-Michel
page.meta: La Régalante, a 275 km cycle route from Nantes to Mont-Saint-Michel via Châteaubriant, Vitré and Fougères: 9 easy stages, bike hire in Nantes.
page.intro: La Régalante is a recent cycle route linking Nantes to Mont-Saint-Michel through the heart of the countryside. Its 275 km, split into 9 stages, mostly follow greenways with very little climbing and pass through historic towns.

stages.texte: The Erdre valley and its châteaux.
Greenways and forests in the north of Loire-Atlantique.
Into Brittany and the medieval town of Vitré.
Fougères castle, one of the largest in Europe.
The Normandy hedgerow country, then the finish facing the bay.

highlights: The ramparts of Vitré and Fougères
page.back: Back by coach and train via Pontorson or Rennes, or one-way hire on request.

faq.question: Is La Régalante difficult?
faq.reponse: No: it mostly follows greenways with little climbing. Allow 9 stages of 25 to 35 km on average, or fewer days if you ride further.

itineraires.name: The Brittany Crossing
itineraires.short: Via the coast, Rennes and Saint-Malo
itineraires.alt: A cyclist on an e-bike on a quiet country road
itineraires.desc: The big trip to Mont-Saint-Michel: the estuary and Guérande, the Vilaine to Redon, Rennes, then the Rance valley, Dinan and the Emerald Coast.

page.h1: The Brittany Crossing, from Nantes to Mont-Saint-Michel
page.title: Brittany Crossing by Bike from Nantes (485 km) | Bike'N Tour
page.meta: The Brittany Crossing by bike: 485 km from Nantes to Mont-Saint-Michel via Guérande, Redon, Rennes, Dinan and Saint-Malo. Stages, tips and bike hire.
page.intro: The big cycling trip to Mont-Saint-Michel: the Loire estuary and Guérande, the Vilaine to Redon, Rennes, the Rance valley, Dinan, then the Emerald Coast and the bay. A varied route of almost 500 km.

stages.texte: The Vélidéale along the estuary.
La Baule and the salt marshes.
The Vilaine, Arzal and La Roche-Bernard.
The Vilaine towpath.
The Ille-et-Rance canal.
The Rance valley.
Cancale, the bay and the finish at the Mont.

page.back: Train back from Rennes or Saint-Malo, or one-way hire on request.

faq.question: How long does the Brittany Crossing take?
faq.reponse: Allow 8 to 10 days for the 485 km, at 50 to 60 km a day. An e-bike is recommended for the hillier sections.

itineraires.name: The Nantes–Brest Canal
itineraires.short: Towpaths all the way to Finistère
itineraires.alt: Two cyclists setting off from the centre of Nantes
itineraires.desc: Locks, lock-keepers' cottages and perfectly flat towpaths: the canal crosses inland Brittany from Nantes to Finistère. You can ride just part of it, as far as Redon or Josselin.

page.title: The Nantes–Brest Canal by Bike: Stages | Bike'N Tour
page.meta: The Nantes–Brest Canal by bike from Nantes: towpaths via Redon, Josselin and Pontivy (≈ 360 km). A weekend to Redon or the full trip.
page.intro: Locks, lock-keepers' cottages and perfectly flat towpaths: the Nantes–Brest Canal crosses inland Brittany. Ride it over a weekend as far as Redon, or make it a big trip all the way to Finistère.

stages.texte: The Erdre and its châteaux.
The canal through hedgerow country, ideal for a weekend.
Malestroit and Josselin castle.
The Blavet valley.
Lac de Guerlédan.
The Aulne and the finish in Finistère.

page.back: Train from Redon to Nantes (about 45 min) for the weekend, or back from Quimper or Brest; one-way hire on request.

faq.question: Can I cycle the Nantes–Brest Canal in a weekend?
faq.reponse: Yes: from Nantes to Redon in 2 days, with a train back from Redon.

itineraires.name: The Nantes Vineyards
itineraires.short: A weekend between the Sèvre and Muscadet country
itineraires.alt: Cyclists on a quiet lane in the Nantes vineyards
itineraires.desc: The perfect weekend right on Nantes' doorstep: the Muscadet hillsides, the Sèvre Nantaise and Clisson, with its castle and Italian feel. Quiet lanes and tracks, perfect on a gravel bike.

page.title: Nantes Vineyards by Bike: Nantes – Clisson | Bike'N Tour
page.meta: A cycling weekend in the Nantes Vineyards: the Sèvre Nantaise, Vertou, Clisson and the Muscadet hillsides (≈ 80 km loop). Gravel bike hire in Nantes.
page.intro: The perfect weekend right on Nantes' doorstep: the banks of the Sèvre Nantaise, the Muscadet hillsides and Clisson, with its medieval fortress and Italian feel. Quiet lanes and tracks, perfect on a gravel bike.

stages.texte: The banks of the Sèvre, the Chaussée des Moines at Vertou and the vineyards (37 km).
Back via Vallet and the Muscadet hillsides, with a wine tasting along the way.

highlights: The Chaussée des Moines at Vertou
page.back: Loop back to Nantes, or the TER train from Clisson to Nantes in 20 minutes.

faq.question: Can I cycle from Nantes to Clisson in a day?
faq.reponse: Yes: 37 km along the banks of the Sèvre, with a TER train back from Clisson.
